questions.stem: Why does changing the shape of an enzyme's active site prevent it from functioning?

options.text: The enzyme is broken down into individual amino acids
The enzyme becomes too large to fit inside the cell
The substrate can no longer bind to the active site because it is no longer complementary in shape
The enzyme starts catalysing a different reaction instead

questions.explanation: Enzymes work because their active site has a specific shape that is complementary to the substrate. If the active site shape changes, the substrate can no longer fit, so enzyme-substrate complexes cannot form and the reaction is not catalysed.
